speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Instead, to reduce their risk of committing violent acts again after release, we try to address the underlying issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They learn to address negative thinking patterns that lead them to violence, better regulate their emotions and resolve conflicts without resorting to violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Members of the public who are in any danger of harm are advised to call "999" for assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The National Anti-Violence Helpline, "1800 777 0000", which is manned by trained social workers, is also available 24/7 for members of the public to seek help or report on violence.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I asked the Parliamentary Question (PQ) and my intention is actually to seek clarification on a process whereby we can prevent further stigmatisation; and at the same time, promote rehabilitation and reconciliation between the ex-offender and the family.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Back in December 2021, there was a case of domestic violence involving someone, the perpetrator who had breached bail conditions.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, what would the Ministry be conducting to do, to help in the reconciliation process of our ex-offenders?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: By the way, I do not like the word "ex-offenders".

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think we should call them "overcomers" – they would overcome the challenge of their checkered past.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, we also engage the perpetrators to connect with family, and also to encourage him or her to better understand what are the avenues, how they can overcome such behaviour.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This, in itself, we want them to respectfully, resolve their conflict and to reduce the risk of family violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, what we hope to do, is to increase awareness of and strengthen societal attitudes against family violence, and enhance preventive efforts for persons at risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And, also, we want to develop more avenues to make it easier for survivors and the community to report family violence and get immediate help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to work with community partners to tackle family violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, everyone can play a part in breaking the cycles of abuse and neglect.
